tips.title: Removing Old Paint from Plastic Kit Parts
tips.text: To remove old paint from plastic kit parts, first soften it using a heat gun like the Mr. Hobby Heat Gun. Once paint starts blistering, use a toothbrush or brass brush to scrub off paint chips. For stubborn areas, apply Citadel Paint Stripper and leave for 15 minutes before scrubbing. Rinse with warm water and let dry before sanding smooth with fine grit sandpaper.

tips.title: Fixing Broken Photo-Etch Parts
tips.text: Broken photo-etch parts can be repaired using CA (Cyanoacrylate) glue like Tamiya Extra Thin Cement. Apply a small amount on the inside of the break, join the parts, and hold in place for 30 seconds. Allow to cure for 24 hours. For a stronger bond, use Super Glue and apply a small amount of Tamiya Panel Line Accent Color to match the part's color.

tips.title: Recovering Clogged Airbrushes
tips.text: To recover a clogged Iwata airbrush, disassemble and soak the nozzle and needle in Vallejo Airbrush Thinner for 15 minutes. Use a needle cleaner to scrub the needle, then reassemble and test with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner. If still clogged, disassemble again, dip the needle in Enamel Thinner, reassemble, and test with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner until clear. Clean regularly to prevent clogs.

tips.title: Fixing Paint Reactions/Bubbling
tips.text: Paint reactions and bubbling can occur due to humidity or incompatible paints. To fix, lightly sand the affected area with fine grit sandpaper, wipe with Vallejo Airbrush Thinner, and let dry. Apply a thin layer of Vallejo Surface Primer, let dry, then apply the intended paint. To prevent, ensure paints are compatible, avoid high humidity, and use suitable airbrush pressures (around 15-20 psi for Vallejo paints).

tips.title: Avoiding Frost from Rattle Cans
tips.text: Frosting from rattle cans occurs due to condensation. To avoid, warm the can in warm water for 10 minutes, shake well, then test spray on a scrap piece of paper before painting the model. Avoid spraying in cold temperatures or humid conditions. Always shake the can well before use and test spray.
